newsitem.title: USA: Miami radio talk show host claims AIDS is a myth.
newsitem.headline: Miami radio talk show host claims AIDS is a myth.

text.p: South Florida health officials voiced concern on Monday that a group of radio talk show hosts was telling the local Haitian community that AIDS was a myth and that sufferers should stop taking medication.

"They are saying things like the disease of AIDS does not exist ... that the people who discovered the virus are liars," said Georges Metellus, director of disease surveillance for the Dade County Public Health Unit.

Public health officials feared that the talk show hosts were winning converts in a community where suspicion of authority is common. Some AIDS treatment centres reported that patients have halted treatment and stopped seeing doctors, Metellus said.
"There are some people who are believing it," he said.

Metellus said the hosts of the talk show, aired on Miami's AM radio station WLQY and aimed at the city's large Haitian population, also said that condoms were ineffective and that AZT, a drug used to treat AIDS, "kills people."

According to the U.S. Centres for Disease Control, Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome has killed 342,000 people in the United States and an estimated 650,000 to 900,000 were living with AIDS or HIV, the virus that causes AIDS.
Henri-Claude Saint-Fleur, one of the talk show hosts, said he told listeners that scientists used fake data to prove the existence of AIDS.
"What I said is that nobody can prove that HIV can cause a disease. HIV doesn't cause what we call AIDS," said Saint-Fleur, a Miami psychologist.

Saint-Fleur said scientists had simply "gathered" the symptoms of a host of ailments and called them AIDS, alleging that drug companies were exploiting the myth for profit. He also said he told people not to use AZT.
"People get worse when they take the medication for HIV. We know this," he said. "A lot of people are dying. They are killed by the medication."
Metellus said public health officials were trying to counter the talk show by appearing on other radio programmes to educate Haitians on the dangers of AIDS and the need for condom use.
